name: MARC catheter
full_name: MARC (magnetically assisted remote-controlled) catheter steered by tip-coil current in the MRI field
group: Hetts, Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging, UCSF
versions: 2013: microcatheter tip deflection protocol (hetts2013_magnetically, JoVE); 2014: 2 mm catheter with a solenoid tip coil, foot pedal delivers +/-300 mA (losey2014_magnetically); 2015: 1.6 mm laser-lithographed dual-axis saddle coils, 1.5 T and 3 T (moftakhar2015_new); 2016: intramural copper-braided catheter with a saddle coil, in-room current cart (lillaney2016_endovascular)
target_anatomy: interventional MRI: abdominal aortic branch catheterization, renal artery embolization
devices_driven: own MARC microcatheters: 2 mm with solenoid coil at the tip (losey2014_magnetically abstract); 1.6 mm with double-saddle coils (moftakhar2015_new abstract)
n_dof_detail: tip deflection in 1 axis (2014) or 2 axes (2015); advance and twist by hand
translation_detail: magnetic (Lorentz torque on the current-carrying tip coil in the MRI main field); insertion by hand
rotation_detail: tip deflection set by coil current direction and magnitude
haptics_leader: no: foot pedal (losey2014_magnetically) or in-room cart (lillaney2016_endovascular)
imaging_compat: real-time MRI at 1.5 T (bSSFP) and 3 T; compared with x-ray fluoroscopy
validation_detail: 3 farm pigs (43 +/- 2 kg): MR-guided MARC renal artery embolization with the contralateral kidney under x-ray; embolization successful in all 6 kidneys (lillaney2016_endovascular abstract); in vitro cryogel abdominal aortic phantom: 192/240 (80%) turns with magnetic assistance vs 144/240 (60%) without (losey2014_magnetically abstract)
key_numbers: tip current 300 mA (losey2014_magnetically); MR-guided catheterization 93 +/- 56 s vs 60 +/- 22 s under x-ray (lillaney2016_endovascular); inexperienced operators 67% (1.5 T) and 75% (3 T) successful turns vs 76% under x-ray (moftakhar2015_new)
